_comment_elevation_reversals: DEM under-sample fixes found via `npm run check:elevation` and confirmed on the topo map via the map debug tool's flow arrows. Each pair was a piste reversed because our SRTM sample read one endpoint too low; corrected to the Terrarium DEM values (which matched the topo reads). Several were near-flat mis-samples that showed spurious both-way arrows and become clean one-way descents once corrected. n321004740 is a special case: it sits at a hut/restaurant entrance that is artificially flattened for pedestrian access, so it is set ~level with n7256146736 (2073, within flat tolerance) to KEEP the n7256146736<->n321004740 traverse bidirectional, deliberately overriding the DEM (which reads ~2083).
_comment2: n357164716 (blue 11 Gerent, ~1890 m): we read 1870 while Terrarium reads 1893, and the +-10 m neighbour sweep shows the neighbours only at the -10 m noise floor, so this is a genuine single-node spike. Topology confirms it: at 1870 the node was a pothole — both blue Gerent edges (from n357164713 and from n10717652947) drained INTO it and the only exit was e1060, an unnamed 129 m app-added connector rather than a real run. At 1893 Gerent becomes the clean descending chain n357164713 1908 -> n357164716 1893 -> n10717652947 1877 -> n7231387779 1875, matching the on-the-ground direction (the slope runs n357164716 -> n10717652947).
